Let’s face it, not everyone is lucky enough to have a huge budget for the center piece of their wedding, the cake. It can get super expensive, there are ways around this though to get more bang for your buck!

In your dreams you want a 4 tier wedding cake, fondant with all of the details that go with it but sadly your budget won’t allow it. Contact your cake artist and see what the options are and give them your budget to see what they can come up with! We are here to help and not drain your bank account – though there are some places out there that will!

Dessert bars are a great idea – “what is this?” you ask. It is where you choose a smaller cake, usually 1 to 2 tiers, simply decorated and then you pick other dessert elements to incorporate into it. What you choose may put up the price though depending on servings and what exactly it is.

Below is a list of ideas I have come up with, along with some pictures I have found on the internet.

  • Small cake – 1-2 tiers
  • Cupcakes
  • Mini cupcakes
  • Cake pops (they can get expensive though)
  • Candy in nice jars/containers
  • Cake balls (cake pops without the sticks
  • Brownie bites
  • Mini cheesecakes
  • Mini fruit pies
  • Hand stamped sugar cookies.

Table 1

Table 2

Table 3

How you choose to decorate the table will really set it off, most elements can be found without spending a fortune.

You will need to keep in mind that not everyone is a sweet person so not all will eat dessert (people with small children and older people usually leave early, some may have had too much to drink). The last thing you want to have at the end of the night is a whole bunch of dessert left over.

The last thing I want to talk about is very important. If you are not having a family member or friend doing the dessert bar, then please order all of the elements to the dessert bar from one cake artist – if they don’t offer this service and you are unsure if they are willing to, just ask them!

It is important to get all of your sweets through one person, (not because the cake artist can lose money) but because of word of mouth. I’ll use this example.

The cake and cake balls were purchased through your cake artist, your mini cupcakes were purchased through a grocery store chain and your brownies were made by Aunt Maybelle.

The cake and cake balls were great, the mini cupcake frosting was greasy and unpleasant and Aunt Maybelle went a little heavy-handed with the baking powder leaving the brownies with a slight metallic taste (yes that is what happens with too much baking powder).

Now your guests only know that “X business cake artist” provided all the goodies, as a result people are now only talking about the bad tasting things and relating that back to the cake artist. This can be extremely damaging to a business, as we all know – word of mouth travels like wildfire and once it is out there, there is no taking it back.

So for a dessert bar, please get all the elements from one place, contact your cake artist to see if they can do things that will fit in with your budget (if they can’t look around) and lastly if your cake artist can do exactly what you need, please give them plenty of time to organize everything. Baking is a lot of work and getting the details just right takes even longer.

The best bit is, all of the information above can be used for other celebrations, baby showers, birthdays, work events, quinceañeras etc.
Weddings (or other celebrations) on a budget!
